Link failed queries to protected retrieval traces and source previews.
Show example-set size and confidence before presenting a change as improvement.
python: Store immutable dataset, judgment, run, configuration, and result versions.
Calculate retrieval metrics from canonical evidence judgments before calling the generator.
Add CI gates for zero leakage, required recall, citation, latency, and drift thresholds.

caseStudy.situation: A new embedding model raises average nDCG but misses payment codes and leaks one forbidden test record.
walkthrough: The aggregate chart looks better.
The identifier slice shows lower Recall@K.
The permission slice records a critical forbidden-result failure.
The promotion gate rejects the candidate despite the average gain.
caseStudy.result: Acme avoids trading exact-code reliability and security for a misleading average improvement.
caseStudy.danger: Optimizing only an average answer score hides weak slices, data leakage, and the stage that actually regressed.
caseStudy.takeaway: Separate stages, publish slices, keep baselines fixed, and let critical controls veto averages.

lessons.lab: Design twelve golden queries across six slices. Define relevant evidence, no-answer expectations, and one metric gate for each stage.
lessons.checkpoint: Why should retrieval be evaluated before generation?
lessons.answer: Because a generator cannot reliably recover missing evidence, and separate retrieval metrics reveal whether the failure occurred before answering.
glossary: Golden query - reviewed evaluation question with evidence expectations
Recall@K - fraction of needed evidence found in top K
Drift - measured change from an established baseline

lessons.title: Capstone: the Acme Knowledge Fabric
lessons.diagramPrompt: Create a complete left-to-right architecture. SOURCES: POLICY, CASE API, PAYMENT SQL, ATTACHMENTS. INTAKE: REGISTER, VERSION, PARSE, OCR, PROVENANCE. INDEXES: LEXICAL, VECTOR, VISUAL, GRAPH, STRUCTURED. QUERY: PLAN, AUTHORIZE, HYBRID, RERANK, PACK. POLICY: CITE, CONFLICT, CLARIFY, ABSTAIN. OPERATIONS below: PROMOTE, CACHE, EVAL, TRACE, DELETE. Output ANSWER WITH EVIDENCE to MAYA.
lessons.alt: The complete Acme Knowledge Fabric connects governed sources, versioned multimodal intake, tenant-safe complementary indexes, authorized retrieval and evidence packing, citation and conflict policy, and operational release and evaluation controls before returning an evidenced answer to Maya.
lessons.outcome: Assemble the entire knowledge layer into one explainable contract that future Next.js and Python projects can implement with equivalent fixtures.
lessons.explanation: The Acme Knowledge Fabric is a data product with owners, versions, contracts, and measurable releases. Sources enter only through approved registers and immutable versions. Parsing preserves layout and multimodal provenance. Complementary indexes remain derived and replaceable. Every query produces an auditable plan and allowed scope before hybrid search, reranking, diversity, and evidence packing. The answer layer cites claims, preserves conflict, asks for clarification, or abstains. Promotion, cache versioning, reconciliation, evaluation, tracing, and deletion keep the system trustworthy after launch.
trace: Register authoritative sources and immutable versions.
Create layout, text, visual, graph, and structured evidence records with lineage.
Resolve identity and authorization before every candidate source.
Build a diverse temporal evidence packet through hybrid retrieval and reranking.
Return cited claims, conflict, clarification, or abstention and record the complete manifest.
lessons.analogy: It is like a modern research library, evidence court, and release pipeline working as one system with separate accountable desks.
nextjs: Use App Router pages for sources, versions, search traces, evaluations, and case answers.
Keep authorization, retrieval, source previews, and promotion controls in server boundaries.
Render a uniform evidence experience from a stack-neutral JSON contract.
python: Use FastAPI for typed evidence endpoints and workers for intake and evaluation.
Keep adapters for parsers, retrievers, rerankers, stores, and graphs behind stable interfaces.
Run the same golden fixtures and evidence-policy scenarios as the future TypeScript stack.

caseStudy.situation: Maya asks for a refund while the current policy, old case note, scanned attachment, and payment ledger disagree.
walkthrough: The source register assigns authority and the temporal plan selects the correct versions.
Authorization restricts all candidate sources before hybrid retrieval.
The packet includes the governing rule, payment fact, attachment confidence, and conflicting note.
The answer explains current eligibility, discloses the earlier contradiction, and cites exact permitted evidence.
caseStudy.result: Maya receives a decision-ready evidence packet rather than a confident paragraph assembled from uncontrolled similarity search.
caseStudy.danger: A knowledge system fails when any one of ownership, permissions, versions, retrieval quality, citation, conflict policy, or operations is treated as someone else's problem.
caseStudy.takeaway: The capstone is complete only when every claim can be reproduced from an authorized source version and every failure has a visible safe outcome.

lessons.lab: Produce the Acme Knowledge Fabric design pack: source authority map, intake contract, chunk design, index topology, query plan, evidence schema, temporal policy, evaluation set, promotion runbook, and deletion test.
lessons.checkpoint: What is the single most important output of the Acme Knowledge Fabric?
lessons.answer: A bounded, authorized, versioned evidence packet whose claims and citations can be reproduced, challenged, and evaluated.
glossary: Knowledge fabric - governed system connecting sources to evidence
Evidence policy - rules for authority, time, conflict, and support
Release manifest - recorded configuration and checks for a promoted knowledge version
